chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Ahmad b. Ishaq b. Buhlul al-Qadi narrated to us in his house in the City of Peace (Baghdad). He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Yazid al-Sada'i narrated to us from Abu Shayba al-Jawhari from Anas b. Malik. He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Promise me six things, and I will guarantee you Paradise: When you speak, do not lie. When you make a promise, do not break it. When you are entrusted, do not betray. Lower your gazes, guard your private parts, and withhold your hands and your tongues."

key_terms.أَبْصَارَكُمْ: Your gazes - refers to looking at what is forbidden
key_terms.الْجَنَّة: Paradise - the ultimate reward in the afterlife
key_terms.فُرُوجَكُمْ: Your private parts - refers to guarding chastity

ai.seo_question: What are the six things the Prophet Muhammad promised would lead to Paradise?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Anas b. Malik, the Prophet Muhammad (s) offers a concise moral contract: six behavioral commitments in exchange for Paradise. The six principles cover speech (truthfulness), commitments (keeping promises), trusts (faithfulness), the gaze (modesty), chastity, and restraining harmful actions of the hands and tongue. This hadith was likely addressed to the general community of believers, establishing foundational ethical standards that were understood as practical daily obligations rather than abstract ideals.
